Wave.name: FastLatencyRelief
Wave.goal: Reduce avoidable latency in the existing cloud-centric path without changing the visible dual-pipeline behavior.

ExecutionOrder.step-1: W1-C4 observability first, so every following change can be measured against baseline.
ExecutionOrder.step-2: W1-C1 STT tuning second, because it is the lowest-risk direct latency reducer.
ExecutionOrder.step-3: W1-C3 client reuse third, because it is a contained hot-path cleanup that reduces jitter before fallback-policy refactoring.
ExecutionOrder.step-4: W1-C2 fallback-policy last, because it changes control flow and should be validated with the improved instrumentation already in place.

Change.summary: Add or normalize stage-level latency and provider markers needed for comparison.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Ensure per-utterance metrics log `stt_ms`, `translate_ms`, `tts_ms`, and `total_ms` in a stable parseable form.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Add translation provider attribution marker such as `provider_used=...` to the accepted translation path.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Normalize emitted runtime evidence so both incoming and outgoing pipelines expose the same measurement surface.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run both pipelines and confirm metrics logs exist for incoming and outgoing paths with provider attribution.

done-when.item: `pipeline_trace.log` contains parseable per-stage metrics for both directions.

Change.summary: Lower Deepgram finalization delay for realtime mode.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Introduce or expose a dedicated realtime endpointing profile in Rust and Elixir runtime config.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Reduce Deepgram finalization settings for short-phrase responsiveness while preserving transcript completion.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Emit the effective endpointing settings in runtime logs so baseline and post-change runs are comparable.

verification-step.runtime-check: Capture at least 10 short-phrase samples per direction and compare `stt_final_ms` to baseline.

done-when.item: Short-phrase p50 `stt_final_ms` improves by at least 300 ms.
Both directions still emit final transcripts reliably.

stop-if.item: Final transcript production becomes unreliable inside the 60s autonomy window.

Change.summary: Remove per-request HTTP client setup from translation hot paths.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Refactor Yandex translation path so the HTTP client is initialized once and reused.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Review translation module constructors to avoid avoidable hot-path object churn.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Preserve the current provider behavior while reducing request setup overhead.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run repeated short-phrase translation samples and compare variance before and after the refactor.

done-when.item: No per-request HTTP client construction remains on the realtime Yandex translation path.
Repeated short translations show lower cold-start variance than baseline.

Change.summary: Replace serial translation fallback with first-success wins for realtime mode.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Change translation control flow so realtime mode does not wait through long serial fallback chains.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Use the first successful provider response and retain provider attribution in logs.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Keep fallback correctness visible through explicit runtime evidence and error markers.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run degraded-network or intentionally slowed-provider scenarios and compare p95 `translate_ms` against baseline.

done-when.item: Slow or blocked Groq no longer delays fallback until full timeout in realtime mode.
`provider_used=...` identifies the winning provider for each accepted translation.
Degraded-network p95 `translate_ms` improves by at least 30 percent versus serial fallback baseline.

stop-if.item: Provider identity is lost from logs.

acceptance-targets.item: Short-phrase p50 `stt_final_ms` improves by at least 300 ms.
Degraded-network p95 `translate_ms` improves by at least 30 percent.
No material regression in transcript completion reliability.
